To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the exchange of referrals leads to the formation of referral networks, that the link structure of these referral networks determines the service selection behavior of the agents in the network, that different referral networks emerge, depending on the actions of the network members, and that authorities emerge in referral networks, which are agents that are trusted by many agents in the network.

(i) the agents' actions can be used to engineer referral networks with desirable properties; (ii) the network topology and the agents' trust models are closely related and can be controlled by controlling the agents' actions; and (iii) the agents' trustworthiness can be inferred from the topology of the referral network.
the exchange of referrals can lead to the emergence of authorities in the referral network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the engineering of self-organizing, trustworthy, and scalable referral networks.
the design of referral networks that can be used for trustworthy service selection in open environments.
developing self-organizing mechanisms for establishing and maintaining trust among autonomous agents in open, dynamic systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more agents there are, the more referrals are exchanged and the more the network structure converges towards an almost fully connected network.
self-organizing networks can be used to establish trust in open, decentralized environments.
referral networks are robust and resilient, but they require a certain level of trust in the agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a referral network can be designed in such a way that the network evolves towards a state where agents trust each other, and the agents can select services with high trustworthiness.

the agents should interact with others based on their perceived trustworthiness and that they should give a referral to others based on their own trustworthiness and the trustworthiness of the others.
self-organizing networks can be designed to achieve desired properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exchange of referrals is a powerful tool for establishing trust in open, autonomous environments.
referral networks can be engineered by controlling the actions of agents.
the agents should be designed to be conservative and that the network should be allowed to grow gradually, so that it can adapt to the dynamics in the environment.
